ac2/no-service-git counts every git process the service process starts during an event with a hundred additional recorded branches, at the point where a process is made, and finds none; the same counter then counts the fixture's own git command, so it is not blind. ac2/responsive holds the real child remover on a FIFO and serves another signed socket packet while the first event remains received. ac2/only-service-descriptors reads the held child's open descriptors: one the service names as its own is closed in the child and one that was only handed down stays open. The service poll set includes the child pipe, and each removal records its worker, source event, hook and ledger owners. ac2/channel-and-api-closed (fix round 2): the service's channel and API each hold a store connection of their own; the service process holds both files open, and the held child, reading its own /proc/self/fd, holds neither, while the descriptor that was only handed down is still open in it.

ac3/oldest-once observes a second record received while the first child is held, then checks their consumed journal order and separate child identities. ac3/oldest-first leaves three records received before any child starts and reads the consumed order from the journal. ac3/one-worker starts a second consumer on the same store and state root while the first one's child is held in a remover: its child does not answer until the first has ended, the record is consumed once, by the first child, with one Signal journal row. ac3/read-again-under-lock: that second child then takes the next received record and not the one it was started for. restart and consumed-refused prove no repeat and a refused duplicate consumed command. packet-replay verifies the original event identity with no journal advance. spool-before-reconcile replays a real signed spool entry in a child and sees its worktree removed before reconcile. recover-after-signal refuses the consumed write after Signal, restarts, and observes one Signal journal record with the item still due for reconcile.

ac4/session-ended removes the exact ended session scratch. host-wide removes dead sessions from another project and no project. live-no-age leaves a live session with old files. unread-stays refuses malformed process facts and an unread process table. safety/session-work-kept plants a repository with its only commit at the scratch locator and observes it intact after session ended. ac4/ended-while-alive-held sends session ended for a session whose client (a real process) is alive: the scratch stays, the item is deferred as in_use by rule 3 with the event that refused it, and the consumed record names it as held, client_alive. ac4/re-judged-at-client-exit: with the clock stopped, the service poll set holds one process descriptor that stays quiet while the client lives; when the client ends, exactly one more session ended record (hook client-exit, after the first) is written and consumed, and the scratch is removed under that record. ac4/held-across-restart: a consumer that starts again holds the client of a scratch left deferred that way, and removes the scratch at its end. ac4/exited-before-collected (fix round 2): the client is ended and its parent, this suite, does not collect it; its stat reads state Z with the recorded start time, and with the clock stopped one client-exit record is written and consumed and the scratch is removed under it while the client is still uncollected. The same number with another start time is not exited, and a live client is not.

assumptions: All criteria remain pending until the full gate and independent review. The selftest runs are partial evidence, not a verification claim.

The service uses the existing explicit space wiring. The suite supplies that Ledger and its declarations; automatic construction of a Ledger from installation files is not added or proven here. serve wires the hook listener, startup pass and child pipe when that Ledger is supplied. No live installation was started.

The act predicate, free-space reading, declarations and membership records are fixtures. Journal signatures are deterministic stand-ins; hook packet signatures are real OpenSSH signatures. The ordinary act switch still refuses the unbuilt VELDO-0332 and VELDO-0339 checks.

The process table is a private fixture, with a link to the suite process for the live-session row. The unread-table row supplies an unread mount-table answer. No real Docker engine, data volume, installed process reader or protected data was touched.

The CLI event verb still supplies an incomplete verb/session envelope and is refused as invalid_input:emitter. Its creator wiring and session hooks are outside this ticket. released can be recorded but removes nothing here; VELDO-0335 supplies that behavior.

The recovery row stops after the committed Signal by refusing the consumed write, not by delivering SIGKILL. Recovery marks the event consumed without signalling again; due or removing items remain for the existing reconcile path and its keep checks. A service replacement while a live worker holds the lock is exercised by a second consumer in the same process and on the same ledger object, not by a second service process.
The heavy suite 151 was not run. Its four edited event-envelope expectations are exercised directly in suite 153. Suite 86_veldo_0127 and all captures were left untouched.

The teeth stage ran for finding 323 only, with four workers under nice 10, on a host under load from other runs. policy_check.py and the full gate were not run. No fix validation record is in this bundle: the review, its validation and the gate are the lead's.

Fix round 2, descriptors (lead decision): the store connections the service's channel and API hold are in the list a worker closes, with the lock, the two listeners, the launch, provisioner and Docker pipes and the service's own connection. In serve the API works on the channel's connection, so the two names are one connection there; the row gives each a connection of its own so that each has a falsifier. What the API opens within one call (a hint socket, its log) is closed within that call and is not in the list. serve was not started in any row.

Fix round 2, session ended (lead decision): a client that ended and is not yet collected by its parent has exited. The worker reads state Z and the recorded start time from the client's stat and requires that no task of it still runs; for a session ended event rule 4 then does not count that client as an unread process. Only the clients of the scratch the event selected are judged this way: any other uncollected process is still unread for rule 4, as before. No row plants a client whose first thread ended while another task of it runs (it is not exited by this reading, and stays deferred), nor a real reused process number (the row gives the same number with another start time to the function directly).

Fix round, session ended: a scratch whose recorded process cannot be read is still not selected, and the record names it as held, process_unread; no row plants that case for a session ended record. A client that cannot be held by a process descriptor is written to the observation log as space_client_unwatched and is not watched; no row plants that either.
The startup bootstrap (Service.space at service start, the real reconcile) is VELDO-0315 AC7 and is not built here.
rollback: Revert the change. Hook events remain spooled or received, with no new consumer removals.
